literal: Valor and honor, excellent path-following, and trustworthiness—thus these four indeed are protection for the army.
translation: Valor, honor, following the noble path of tradition, and trustworthiness—these four are the true safeguards of an army.
modern: வீரம், மானம், முன்னோர் காட்டிய நல்வழியில் நடத்தல், மற்றும் நம்பிக்கைக்குரிய தன்மை ஆகிய இந்த நான்குமே ஒரு படைக்குப் பாதுகாப்பாகும்.
explanation: This couplet outlines the four essential qualities that protect and sustain an army. First is 'மறம்' (valor or bravery in battle) and second is 'மானம்' (honor, which prevents soldiers from retreating in disgrace). Third is 'வழிச்செலவு', which refers to following the disciplined, noble traditions of warfare established by ancestors. Fourth is 'தேற்றம்', meaning trustworthiness or reliability, which ensures loyalty to the leadership. Together, these moral and behavioral traits form the ultimate defense (ஏமம்) of an army, far exceeding mere physical strength.
